prompt.context: Our client is a major US television network. They are trying to figure out how much to bid for the exclusive right to broadcast the Winter Olympics Games, which will take place in four years. The Winter Olympics are a huge deal and will require a significant amount of capital to secure the rights, so our client has brought us in to help them figure out the right bid amount after considering all relevant factors.
prompt.question: How much should our client bid for the exclusive right to broadcast the Winter Olympics?

clarifying_info.a: No subscription revenue. The network can keep 100% of advertising revenue.
Ad rates are $400k per 30-second ad for prime time (weekends, and weekdays 1900–2300) and $200k per 30-second ad for non-prime time.

clarifying_info.q: How much advertising time is allowed per hour?
clarifying_info.a: Market research shows you can include no more than 10 minutes of advertising per hour.
Yes, $1M per hour of broadcast time.

clarifying_info.q: How should we account for the time value of money?
clarifying_info.a: There is a 4-year lag for receipt of revenue. WACC is 10%.

exhibits.title: Winter Olympics Schedule
exhibits.shows: A grid showing the broadcast schedule for the 16-day Winter Olympics. Day 1 is the Opening Ceremony (Friday), Days 2–15 are Main Events (mix of weekdays and weekends), and Day 16 is the Closing Ceremony (Saturday). Each day shows hourly time slots from 0800 to 2300 with specific sports assigned to each slot.

data.opening_ceremony: Day 1, Friday: 2000–2100 Opening commentary, 2100–2200 Opening ceremony, 2200–2300 Opening speeches (3 hours prime time)
data.main_events_weekday: Days 2–15 include 10 weekday broadcast days: 0900–1500 non-prime (6 hrs), 1900–2300 prime (4 hrs)
data.main_events_weekend: Days 2–15 include 4 weekend broadcast days: 0800–1800 (10 hrs prime time)
data.closing_ceremony: Day 16, Saturday: 2000–2100 Closing commentary, 2100–2200 Closing speeches, 2200–2300 Closing ceremony (3 hours prime time)

framework: Revenues: Calculate total advertising revenue by segment (prime time weekdays, non-prime time weekdays, weekends, opening/closing ceremonies)
Costs: Identify production costs ($482M), opportunity costs ($1M/hr x total broadcast hours), and time value of money (4-year NPV discount at 10% WACC)
NPV: Revenues minus total costs, discounted back 4 years to determine maximum NPV-justified bid
Intangibles: Consider strategic benefits (new viewers, prestige, cross-promotion) and risks that could adjust the bid above or below NPV
Recommendation: Set bid at or around NPV, adjusted for intangibles and competitive dynamics (game theory of bid process)

questions.prompt: Calculate total advertising revenue from the Winter Olympics broadcast.
questions.guidance: Candidate must read the schedule exhibit carefully, segment days by type (weekday prime, weekday non-prime, weekend, opening/closing), compute ad slots per segment, and multiply by the correct rate. Strong candidates work systematically and arrive at $928M.

math.setup: 10 min ads/hr = 20 slots of 30-sec ads per hour. Prime rate = $400k/slot, non-prime = $200k/slot.
steps: Weekday prime time (M–F, 1900–2300): 10 weekdays x 4 hrs/day x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $400k = $320M
Weekday non-prime (M–F, 0900–1500): 10 weekdays x 6 hrs/day x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $200k = $240M
Weekend (4 days, 0800–1800, all prime): 4 days x 10 hrs/day x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $400k = $320M
Opening/Closing ceremonies (2 days x 3 hrs prime): 2 x 3 x 10 x 2 x $400k = $48M

questions.prompt: Calculate total costs and profit from the Olympics broadcast.
questions.guidance: Candidate must identify three cost components: production costs (given), opportunity cost (broadcast hours x $1M/hr), and time value of money. Strong candidates correctly calculate total broadcast hours for opportunity cost.

math.setup: Opportunity cost = total broadcast hours x $1M/hr. Broadcast hours: Opening/Closing ceremonies = 2 days x 3 hrs = 6 hrs; Main event days = 14 days x 10 hrs/day = 140 hrs. Total = 146 hrs.
steps: Opportunity cost: (2 days x 3 hrs x $1M/hr) + (14 days x 10 hrs x $1M/hr) = $6M + $140M = $146M

questions.prompt: Calculate the NPV of the project given the 4-year lag and 10% WACC.
questions.guidance: Candidate must apply a 4-year discount factor. Strong candidates compute 1.10^4 = 1.4641 and are willing to round to 1.5 when prompted, yielding a clean $200M NPV.

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the NPV calculation, what intangible benefits and risks should the network consider when setting its bid?

categories.name: Strategic Benefits
ideas: Access to new viewers who may not normally watch the network
Prestige and brand enhancement from being the exclusive Olympics broadcaster
Ability to use air time to promote other network programming and upcoming shows
Opportunities for product tie-ins and supplemental revenue streams
Strengthened advertiser relationships through premium inventory

categories.name: Risks and Downside Factors
ideas: Bid competition — other networks may bid aggressively, inflating the price beyond NPV
Execution risk — production costs could overrun the $482M estimate
Viewership risk — ratings may underperform if Winter Olympics interest declines
Revenue risk — actual ad sales may fall short of the 10-min/hr maximum fill assumption
Geopolitical or scheduling risk — event cancellation or postponement

categories.name: Bid Process / Game Theory
ideas: The winning bid must exceed competitors, not just exceed NPV
Knowing competitors' reservation values affects optimal bid strategy
Overpaying erodes value even if the broadcast is profitable
Incremental value of intangibles should increase the bid above NPV

recommendation: Bid approximately $200M, which equals the calculated NPV of the project
Intangible benefits (new viewers, cross-promotion, prestige, supplemental revenue) justify bidding at or modestly above NPV rather than below it
The bid should not deviate far from $200M without strong justification tied to specific intangible value estimates
risks: Overpaying if intangibles are overestimated or do not materialize
Competitive dynamics may force the winning bid above $200M, making the investment NPV-negative
Execution risk on production costs could reduce actual profit below $300M
next_steps: Assess competitive landscape — identify which other networks are likely bidders and their financial capacity
Refine revenue assumptions — model sensitivity to ad fill rates and potential rating scenarios
Quantify intangibles — estimate the dollar value of cross-promotion benefits and new viewer acquisition
Develop a bid range and walk-away price before entering negotiations
